answer.answer: Yes, water is taking over Wadi Field. The field's water cut (the share of water in what the wells bring up) has climbed from about 0.62 in January 2026 to about 0.71 in November 2026, while oil output has slipped from about 8,900 to 7,600 barrels a day over the same period [P1]. The rise is steady month on month, which points to the water flood pushing more water through the reservoir rather than a one-off event.

Before normal operation resumes, the procedure requires a sand cleanout and a well test confirming sand-free production.
